answer.rationale:
The competitor's entry pricing creates the loudest pull toward promotional_pricing, but the only memory supporting that direction (memory_73) carries an explicit self-flagged defect: the readout pooled two cohorts after a mid-test redefinition, so its 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' may be an artifact of the pooling rather than a real effect. Discount-led acquisition also carries the largest downstream risk against the primary objective — it can import price-sensitive, low-retention accounts and reset price expectations, converting a revenue lift into a durable margin and churn liability. That is the wrong instrument to commit a non-recurring slot to on compromised evidence.

The measured internal deterioration is in onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), and these are likely causally linked: onboarding completion is upstream of first meaningful action. Two independent memories converge here (memory_86 on shortening onboarding lifting completion and time-to-value; memory_31 on signup field reduction producing a durable first-week activation lift), and neither carries a noted methodological caveat. memory_91 (activation messaging) is credible but treats the symptom downstream of the funnel break; fixing the upstream constriction should propagate into activation as well. memory_44 (enterprise sales-assist) and memory_57 (referrals) address segments that are not the ones bleeding.

Verification spend: memory_73 because it is the flagged record and the one that would most change my decision if the defect turns out to be immaterial (a clean cohort-level readout showing genuine SMB lift would make a guarded pricing test defensible against a live competitive threat). memory_86 because it is the load-bearing evidence for what I actually intend to do, and inherited reliability is not the same as verified reliability — I want to confirm the effect was on completion and time-to-value in a comparable self-serve population, not a narrow segment, before scaling.

Scale is standard_experiment, not broad rollout: the supporting evidence is 45-64 days old and the current declines are new, so the underlying cause may differ from the conditions under which those lifts were observed. I hold the causal onboarding-to-activation link as a hypothesis, not established fact, and will instrument completion and first-week activation separately so a null result is legible rather than absorbed. If memory_73 verifies clean and memory_86 does not, I would revisit toward a small_guarded_test on pricing with explicit retention and margin guardrails.
